task_1.title: Decouple JWT claim validation from signature verification
task_1.description: PyJWT 2.1.0 allows applications to decode tokens without verifying the JWT signature while still optionally enforcing standard claim validation. Claim checks are no longer skipped solely because signature verification is disabled, but they remain off by default in that mode unless the caller explicitly enables them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT decoding can validate configured standard claims even when signature verification is disabled, without turning claim validation into a mandatory default for unsigned decoding.

expectation.grounded: `jwt.decode()` should always run claim validation using the merged decode options rather than skipping validation whenever `verify_signature` is `False`. When signature verification is disabled, verification of `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `aud`, and `iss` should default to disabled unless the caller explicitly enables the corresponding claim check. If a caller enables one of those checks while `verify_signature` is `False`, decoding should enforce that claim and raise the normal public validation failure for an invalid claim. The `algorithms` argument should still be required only when signature verification is enabled.
expectation.conceptual: Applications should be able to inspect a JWT without verifying its signature and still opt into validating specific standard claims. Disabling signature verification should no longer force all claim validation off, but unsigned decoding should remain permissive by default unless the caller asks for a specific claim check.

constraints.grounded: Do not make unsigned decoding fail by default on `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `aud`, or `iss` when `verify_signature` is `False` and no claim-specific verification flags are enabled. Do not introduce a new requirement to provide `algorithms` when signature verification is disabled. Preserve existing signed-decoding behavior by continuing to apply claim validation from the merged default and per-call decode options.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should add optional claim enforcement for unsigned decoding without breaking callers that only disable signature verification to read token contents. Existing signed-token decoding behavior should remain consistent, and enabling a claim check should have the same user-visible effect regardless of whether signature verification is on.

behavior: Decoding should apply claim-validation logic even when signature verification is disabled.
When signature verification is disabled and no claim-specific verification options are set, expiration, not-before, issued-at, audience, and issuer checks should remain disabled by default.

When signature verification is disabled and a claim-specific verification option is explicitly enabled, decoding should enforce that claim and reject tokens that violate it with the corresponding public validation error.
The requirement to provide `algorithms` should continue to apply only to signature-verified decoding, not to unsigned decoding that performs claim validation.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller decodes a token with signature verification disabled and does not opt into any claim checks, decoding should return the payload without failing solely because `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `aud`, or `iss` would be invalid.
When a caller decodes a token with signature verification disabled and explicitly enables expiration validation, expired tokens should be rejected with the normal expiration-validation failure.

When a caller decodes a token with signature verification disabled and explicitly enables another supported standard claim check, decoding should enforce that claim instead of accepting the token simply because signature verification is off.
When a caller decodes a token with signature verification enabled and omits `algorithms`, decoding should continue to fail with `DecodeError`.

task_2.title: Clarify canonical unpadded JWK value format
task_2.description: Version 2.1.0 clarifies that JWK values are represented in canonical unpadded Base64URL form. The provided production code diff is empty, so this release item should be treated as a format clarification rather than a runtime behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure JWK-related usage guidance reflects canonical unpadded Base64URL member values, while preserving the same runtime behavior for consumers upgrading from 2.0.1 to 2.1.0.

expectation.grounded: The 2.1.0 release note indicates JWK data should no longer include Base64URL padding, and the provided production code diff introduces no public runtime changes. Upgrading should therefore preserve the existing API and behavior while treating unpadded JWK member values as the expected representation.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should not change how applications behave at runtime, but users should understand that JWK values are expected and described in their standard unpadded Base64URL form.

constraints.grounded: Do not infer new public APIs, parsing rules, warnings, or exception behavior from this release item, because the provided production diff is empty. Existing JWK-related integrations should continue to work the same after the upgrade.
constraints.conceptual: This change must not force code changes or introduce behavioral regressions; it only clarifies the canonical serialized form of JWK values.

behavior: The provided production diff shows no runtime code changes between 2.0.1 and 2.1.0 for this release item.
No new public API surface, error condition, or observable execution path is introduced by the provided code diff.
Release guidance now treats unpadded Base64URL encoding as the canonical representation for JWK values.
acceptance_criteria: When upgrading from 2.0.1 to 2.1.0, existing production behavior for JWK-related flows should remain unchanged.
When users read or exchange JWK values after the upgrade, they should treat unpadded Base64URL values as the expected canonical representation.
The upgrade should not require consumers to adopt new APIs, handle new exceptions, or change existing runtime integration logic solely because of this release item.

task_3.title: Support JWKs without alg while requiring kty
task_3.description: The update allows JWK loading to succeed when a key omits alg by inferring a supported default algorithm from the key type and curve metadata, while also enforcing RFC-compliant validation that every JWK must declare kty and that unsupported or underspecified key metadata is rejected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWK loading accepts supported keys that omit `alg` by deriving the algorithm from the key metadata, and ensure that JWKs without `kty` or with unsupported key type or curve values are rejected as invalid.

expectation.grounded: When `PyJWK` loads JWK data, `kty` must always be present. If neither an explicit algorithm nor a JWK `alg` value is provided, the library should infer the algorithm from `kty` and `crv`: `EC` maps to `ES256` for `P-256` or missing `crv`, `ES384` for `P-384`, `ES512` for `P-521`, and `ES256K` for `secp256k1`; `RSA` maps to `RS256`; `oct` maps to `HS256`; `OKP` with `crv` `Ed25519` maps to `EdDSA`. Missing `kty`, unsupported `kty`, unsupported `crv`, or missing `crv` for `OKP` should raise `InvalidKeyError`.
expectation.conceptual: Applications should be able to load common JWKs from providers that omit `alg` and still get the correct signing algorithm automatically, while malformed or ambiguous keys fail fast with a key validation error instead of being accepted without a determinable algorithm.

constraints.grounded: Do not require `alg` when supported key metadata is sufficient to determine the algorithm. Preserve the precedence of an explicit algorithm argument or a JWK-provided `alg` when present. Do not silently accept JWKs that lack `kty` or use unsupported key type or curve combinations.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand compatibility for valid alg-less JWKs without weakening input validation. Keys that clearly identify a supported algorithm should continue to load, and keys that do not provide enough valid metadata should be rejected rather than guessed.

behavior: `PyJWK` now treats `kty` as mandatory for all JWK inputs, regardless of whether another algorithm source is available.
If no explicit algorithm and no JWK `alg` are provided, `PyJWK` infers a default algorithm from `kty` and `crv` instead of failing immediately for a missing algorithm.
EC JWKs without `alg` use curve-based defaults: `P-256` or missing `crv` selects `ES256`, `P-384` selects `ES384`, `P-521` selects `ES512`, and `secp256k1` selects `ES256K`.
RSA JWKs without `alg` default to `RS256`, `oct` JWKs default to `HS256`, and `OKP` JWKs with `crv` `Ed25519` default to `EdDSA`.
Unsupported `kty`, unsupported `crv`, and missing `crv` for `OKP` are rejected with `InvalidKeyError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a JWK with `kty` `RSA` is loaded without `alg`, it should load successfully and use `RS256`.
When an `EC` JWK is loaded without `alg`, it should use `ES256` for `P-256` or missing `crv`, `ES384` for `P-384`, `ES512` for `P-521`, and `ES256K` for `secp256k1`.
When an `oct` JWK is loaded without `alg`, it should load successfully and use `HS256`.
When an `OKP` JWK with `crv` `Ed25519` is loaded without `alg`, it should load successfully and use `EdDSA`.
When a JWK omits `kty`, it should raise `InvalidKeyError` even if another algorithm source is supplied.
When a JWK uses an unsupported key type, an unsupported curve, or an `OKP` key without `crv`, it should raise `InvalidKeyError`.
When an explicit algorithm argument or a JWK `alg` value is present, the library should use that value instead of inferring a default from `kty`.

task_5.title: Allow EC verification with private keys
task_5.description: The upgrade expands ECDSA JWT verification so callers can supply an elliptic-curve private key where a verification key is accepted. Verification should succeed using the corresponding public component, bringing ECAlgorithm behavior in line with the existing Ed25519 experience and avoiding failures for integrations that only retain the private key object.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that ECDSA token verification accepts an elliptic-curve private key as a valid verification input, so applications can verify signatures with the same key object they already hold and get behavior consistent with other asymmetric algorithms that already allow this.

expectation.grounded: ECAlgorithm.verify must accept either an elliptic-curve public key or an EllipticCurvePrivateKey as the key argument. When an EllipticCurvePrivateKey is provided, verification must be performed against its corresponding public key and preserve the existing verification contract of returning success for valid signatures and failure for invalid signatures.
expectation.conceptual: JWT verification for EC-based algorithms should work whether the caller provides the public key directly or the matching private key object. A valid signature should still verify successfully, and invalid signatures should still be rejected.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to ECAlgorithm verification input handling. Existing support for verification with public keys must remain unchanged, and signature validation outcomes for valid and invalid EC signatures must not regress apart from newly accepting elliptic-curve private keys as equivalent verification material.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden accepted verification inputs without changing normal verification behavior. Existing successful verification flows must continue to work, and the library should not weaken signature rejection rules.

behavior: ECAlgorithm verification accepts elliptic-curve private key objects in addition to elliptic-curve public keys.
When a private key is supplied for EC verification, the library verifies the signature using that key's public component rather than treating the private key as unsupported input.
EC-based verification behavior is aligned with the existing Ed25519 behavior that already permits verification with a private key object.
Valid EC signatures continue to verify successfully, and invalid EC signatures continue to produce a failed verification result.
acceptance_criteria: When an application verifies an EC-signed JWT with ECAlgorithm.verify and passes the corresponding elliptic-curve public key, it should continue to verify valid signatures successfully.
When an application verifies an EC-signed JWT with ECAlgorithm.verify and passes the corresponding elliptic-curve private key, it should verify the same valid signature successfully.
When an application verifies an EC-signed JWT with ECAlgorithm.verify and the signature is not valid for the supplied key material, it should still report verification failure.

When applications migrate from version 2.0.1 to 2.1.0, EC signature verification should no longer fail solely because the caller supplied a compatible elliptic-curve private key instead of the public key.

task_6.title: Default signing-key caching for PyJWKClient
task_6.description: Version 2.1.0 changes PyJWKClient so repeated signing-key lookups can be reused by key ID instead of always triggering another JWKS fetch. This reduces authentication latency for repeated lookups while preserving an explicit opt-out and a configurable cache size for applications with different freshness or memory needs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that repeated PyJWKClient signing-key lookups for the same key ID are cached by default to reduce unnecessary JWKS network requests, while still allowing applications to disable caching or limit cache size when they need different runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: PyJWKClient should expose constructor options cache_keys and max_cached_keys in addition to uri. With cache_keys enabled by default, get_signing_key(kid) should reuse a previously resolved signing key for the same kid on subsequent calls from the same client instance instead of performing another fetch through the JWKS URI. With cache_keys=False, get_signing_key should retain uncached lookup behavior. max_cached_keys should define the upper bound for cached signing-key entries.
expectation.conceptual: By default, signing-key resolution should behave like a per-client cache keyed by key ID so repeated lookups avoid another remote JWKS retrieval. Applications that require fresh lookups every time must be able to opt out, and applications that want bounded memory use must be able to set the cache capacity.

constraints.grounded: The get_signing_key public API and key-selection behavior for a requested kid must remain intact. Caching must be optional through cache_keys=False, and cache capacity control through max_cached_keys must remain part of the public constructor contract. The change must not alter how different kid values are resolved beyond allowing previously resolved results to be reused for matching repeated lookups.
constraints.conceptual: Caching should improve repeated lookup performance without changing which signing key is chosen for a given key ID. Consumers must keep control over whether lookups are cached and how large the cache may grow.

behavior: Creating PyJWKClient with default arguments enables signing-key caching.
After get_signing_key resolves a signing key for a given kid, later calls with the same kid on the same client instance reuse that cached result.
Repeated same-kid lookups served from cache avoid another JWKS retrieval from the configured URI.
Passing cache_keys=False disables this caching and preserves lookup behavior that performs remote resolution on repeated calls.
Passing max_cached_keys configures the maximum number of cached signing-key results retained by the client.
acceptance_criteria: When an application creates PyJWKClient(uri) and resolves a signing key for a kid, a later request for that same kid through the same client should return the signing key without requiring another JWKS fetch.
When an application creates PyJWKClient(uri, cache_keys=False), repeated requests for the same kid should continue to use uncached key resolution behavior.
When different kid values are requested through the same client, signing-key resolution should continue to select keys by the requested kid using the existing public API.
When an application provides max_cached_keys, the client should continue caching repeated lookups while respecting the configured cache capacity.

task_4.title: Support JWKs That Omit alg
task_4.description: Version 2.1.0 allows RFC7517-compliant JWKs to be loaded even when they do not declare an alg value. The library now infers a suitable algorithm from the key type and curve metadata when possible, while rejecting keys whose metadata is missing or unsupported.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWK loading accepts valid keys that omit the `alg` field, derives a usable algorithm from the key's declared type metadata, and rejects malformed or unsupported key descriptions with key-validation errors instead of failing solely because `alg` is absent.

expectation.grounded: `PyJWK` should no longer require a JWK `alg` member when no explicit `algorithm` argument is provided. It should require `kty`, preserve an explicitly supplied `algorithm`, and otherwise infer the algorithm from JWK metadata: `EC` keys map by `crv` to `ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`, or `ES256K`; `RSA` maps to `RS256`; `oct` maps to `HS256`; and `OKP` with `crv` `Ed25519` maps to `EdDSA`. Missing `kty`, missing required `crv` for `OKP`, unsupported `kty`, and unsupported `crv` values should raise `InvalidKeyError`.
expectation.conceptual: Loading a JWK should work even if the key does not name an algorithm, as long as the key metadata clearly identifies one. The library should infer the expected algorithm from the key type information, honor an algorithm explicitly provided by the caller, and reject incomplete or unsupported key metadata with a validation error.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress successful loading of JWKs that already include `alg` or callers that pass `algorithm` explicitly. Only infer an algorithm when none is supplied, and limit inference to the supported `kty` and `crv` combinations introduced by the update. Invalid key metadata should surface as `InvalidKeyError`, not as a generic missing-algorithm failure.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing valid key-loading flows working, but add compatibility for algorithm-less JWKs only when their metadata is sufficient to identify a safe default. Reject keys whose type information is absent or unsupported instead of guessing beyond the documented mappings.

behavior: When a JWK does not contain `alg` and no explicit `algorithm` argument is supplied, the library derives the algorithm from `kty` and, where applicable, `crv`.
For `EC` keys, `P-256` and a missing `crv` resolve to `ES256`, `P-384` resolves to `ES384`, `P-521` resolves to `ES512`, and `secp256k1` resolves to `ES256K`.
For `RSA` keys, the inferred algorithm is `RS256`.
For `oct` keys, the inferred algorithm is `HS256`.
For `OKP` keys, `crv` `Ed25519` resolves to `EdDSA`, while a missing or unsupported `crv` is rejected.
A JWK missing `kty` is rejected with `InvalidKeyError`.
Unsupported `kty` values and unsupported curve values for `EC` or `OKP` keys are rejected with `InvalidKeyError`.
If the caller provides an explicit `algorithm`, that value takes precedence over any inference from the JWK payload.
acceptance_criteria: When loading an RSA JWK that omits `alg`, it should load successfully and be treated as an `RS256` key.

When loading an `EC` JWK that omits `alg`, it should load successfully and choose `ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`, or `ES256K` according to the key's curve, with missing `crv` on `EC` defaulting to `ES256`.
When loading an `oct` JWK that omits `alg`, it should load successfully and be treated as an `HS256` key.
When loading an `OKP` JWK that omits `alg` and declares `crv` `Ed25519`, it should load successfully and be treated as an `EdDSA` key.
When loading a JWK that is missing `kty`, uses an unsupported `kty`, omits `crv` for an `OKP` key, or declares an unsupported `crv` for `EC` or `OKP`, it should fail with `InvalidKeyError`.
When a caller supplies an explicit algorithm value while loading a JWK, the library should honor that value instead of inferring one from the JWK contents.

task_7.title: Expose InvalidKeyError from the top-level jwt API
task_7.description: PyJWT 2.1.0 fixes an omission in 2.0.1 by exposing InvalidKeyError through the public jwt package namespace, so applications can import and handle invalid-key failures consistently with the library's other top-level exception types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the JWT package exposes the missing InvalidKeyError exception from its top-level public API so callers can import and handle invalid-key failures consistently with other JWT exception classes.

expectation.grounded: The public jwt module should re-export InvalidKeyError from the exceptions API and include it in the module's public export set so top-level access to jwt.InvalidKeyError and direct imports of InvalidKeyError from jwt succeed in the same way as other exported JWT exception types.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, applications should be able to access the invalid-key exception from the main JWT package without reaching into a submodule, and it should behave like the rest of the package's public error types.

constraints.grounded: This change should add the missing top-level export only. Existing public exception exports such as InvalidTokenError, InvalidSignatureError, InvalidAudienceError, and InvalidIssuerError must remain available unchanged, and InvalidKeyError should remain the same exception type with the same error semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The update should expand the public error surface without changing how existing JWT exceptions are imported or how invalid-key failures are otherwise interpreted.

behavior: The jwt module exposes InvalidKeyError as a top-level attribute.
InvalidKeyError is included in the jwt module's public export list, so public imports from jwt include it.
Consumers can reference the same InvalidKeyError type from the top-level jwt namespace instead of only through the exceptions module.
acceptance_criteria: When application code imports InvalidKeyError from the jwt package, the import should succeed.
When application code accesses jwt.InvalidKeyError, it should resolve to the library's public invalid-key exception type.
When code relies on other previously exported jwt exception classes, their availability and behavior should remain unchanged after the upgrade.
When invalid-key failures are handled through the top-level jwt namespace, applications should be able to catch the same InvalidKeyError type exposed by the exceptions API.

task_8.title: Add ES256K support and infer algorithms for JWKs without alg
task_8.description: Version 2.1.0 adds support for the ES256K elliptic-curve signing algorithm and updates JWK loading so supported keys can be accepted even when the JWK omits alg, as long as the key type and curve imply a valid default algorithm. Unsupported or malformed key metadata should now fail with explicit key validation errors instead of being treated as an unspecified algorithm.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the library supports ES256K-backed elliptic-curve keys and can load supported JWKs without an explicit alg by deriving the correct default algorithm from the key metadata, while rejecting missing or unsupported key type and curve combinations.

expectation.grounded: The default algorithm set should expose ES256K as a supported cryptography-backed EC algorithm. JWK handling through PyJWK should accept missing alg when the JWK metadata is sufficient to infer it: EC keys should map P-256 to ES256, P-384 to ES384, P-521 to ES512, and secp256k1 to ES256K; RSA keys should default to RS256; oct keys should default to HS256; OKP Ed25519 keys should default to EdDSA. EC JWK parsing should accept secp256k1 coordinates of the expected length and raise InvalidKeyError for missing kty, unsupported kty, unsupported crv, missing OKP crv, or invalid secp256k1 coordinate size.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to use secp256k1 keys with ES256K and supply common JWKs without needing to repeat alg when the key itself already determines the algorithm. The library should choose the expected default algorithm for supported key types and fail clearly when the key metadata is incomplete or unsupported.

constraints.grounded: Existing supported EC curves must keep their current algorithm mappings, and absence of alg must not silently succeed for unknown key types or curves. Only supported OKP Ed25519 keys may infer EdDSA, and secp256k1 acceptance must still enforce valid EC coordinate sizing before a key is constructed.
constraints.conceptual: The new behavior must extend supported key loading without weakening validation. Adding convenience for omitted alg must not guess across unsupported key formats or accept malformed curve parameters.

behavior: ES256K becomes a recognized asymmetric algorithm in the library's default algorithm registry.
EC JWK parsing recognizes the secp256k1 curve and accepts it when the public key coordinates have the required size for that curve.
Creating a PyJWK from a JWK dictionary no longer requires alg when the key type and, where applicable, the curve identify a supported default algorithm.
For EC JWKs without alg, the inferred algorithm depends on crv, including ES256K for secp256k1.
For RSA, oct, and OKP Ed25519 JWKs without alg, PyJWK infers RS256, HS256, and EdDSA respectively.
If kty is missing, if kty is unsupported, if crv is unsupported, if an OKP key omits crv, or if secp256k1 coordinates are invalid, key loading fails with an invalid-key error.
acceptance_criteria: When a user requests the default supported algorithms in an environment with cryptography-backed algorithms available, ES256K should be included as a supported option.
When a JWK for an EC key uses crv secp256k1 and provides valid coordinates, the library should load it successfully and treat it as an ES256K-capable key.

When PyJWK is created from a supported EC, RSA, oct, or OKP Ed25519 JWK that omits alg, it should infer the correct default algorithm from the key metadata instead of failing solely because alg is absent.
When an EC JWK omits alg and uses crv P-256, P-384, P-521, or secp256k1, the inferred algorithm should be ES256, ES384, ES512, or ES256K respectively.
When a JWK is missing kty or uses an unsupported key type or curve, the library should reject it with an invalid-key failure rather than proceeding with an inferred algorithm.
When a secp256k1 JWK provides coordinates with an invalid size, the library should reject the key as invalid.

task_10.title: Add Ed25519 JWK import and export support
task_10.description: Version 2.1.0 adds JWK interoperability for Ed25519 keys so applications using Ed25519Algorithm can serialize supported keys to JWK and load Ed25519 OKP JWK representations back into usable key objects, while rejecting malformed or incompatible key material through the existing key validation path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Ed25519Algorithm supports JWK interoperability for Ed25519 keys, including exporting supported Ed25519 public and private keys to JWK form and loading valid Ed25519 OKP JWK inputs back into usable key objects, while rejecting invalid or incompatible JWK data with key validation errors.

expectation.grounded: Ed25519Algorithm must expose JWK conversion behavior for Ed25519 keys. `to_jwk()` must accept Ed25519 public and private key objects and return a JWK JSON representation using the OKP key type and Ed25519 curve, including the public component and the private component only for private keys. `from_jwk()` must accept either a JSON string or a dictionary representing an OKP Ed25519 JWK, return an Ed25519 public key when only the public component is present, and return an Ed25519 private key when private key material is present. Invalid JSON, unsupported key object types, non-OKP JWKs, non-Ed25519 curves, missing required public key material, or invalid encoded key parameters must raise `InvalidKeyError`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to round-trip Ed25519 keys through JWKs with Ed25519Algorithm. Public keys should export and import as public JWKs, private keys should export and import as private JWKs, and malformed or unsupported inputs should fail with a key validation error instead of producing a usable key.

constraints.grounded: Only Ed25519 OKP JWKs are supported by this behavior. Export must not emit private key material for public keys. Import must not accept non-JSON inputs, incompatible JWK key types or curves, missing public key fields, or invalidly encoded key bytes. Error signaling for unsupported or invalid inputs must use `InvalidKeyError`.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability is limited to valid Ed25519 JWK interoperability. It must preserve the distinction between public-only and private keys, avoid leaking private data when exporting a public key, and consistently reject malformed or non-Ed25519 key descriptions.

behavior: Ed25519Algorithm now supports exporting Ed25519 public keys to JWK JSON with OKP/Ed25519 metadata and the public key component.
Ed25519Algorithm now supports exporting Ed25519 private keys to JWK JSON with OKP/Ed25519 metadata, the public key component, and the private key component.
Ed25519Algorithm now accepts JWK input as either a JSON string or a dictionary.
Importing an OKP JWK for the Ed25519 curve with only public key material returns an Ed25519 public key object.
Importing an OKP JWK for the Ed25519 curve with private key material returns an Ed25519 private key object.
Supplying an unsupported key object to `to_jwk()` raises `InvalidKeyError`.
Supplying invalid JSON, a non-OKP JWK, a non-Ed25519 curve, missing required public key material, or invalid encoded key parameters to `from_jwk()` raises `InvalidKeyError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller passes an Ed25519 public key to `Ed25519Algorithm.to_jwk()`, it should return a JWK JSON representation for an OKP Ed25519 public key and should not include private key material.

When a caller passes an Ed25519 private key to `Ed25519Algorithm.to_jwk()`, it should return a JWK JSON representation for an OKP Ed25519 private key that includes both the public and private key components.
When a caller passes a valid OKP Ed25519 public JWK as a JSON string or dictionary to `Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk()`, it should return a usable Ed25519 public key object.
When a caller passes a valid OKP Ed25519 private JWK as a JSON string or dictionary to `Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk()`, it should return a usable Ed25519 private key object.

When a caller exports a supported Ed25519 key with `to_jwk()` and then imports the result with `from_jwk()`, the returned key should preserve the same public-only versus private-key capability as the original input.

When `Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk()` receives malformed JSON, a non-dictionary non-string input, a JWK with the wrong key type or curve, a JWK missing the public key component, or invalid encoded key material, it should raise `InvalidKeyError`.
When `Ed25519Algorithm.to_jwk()` receives an object that is not an Ed25519 public or private key, it should raise `InvalidKeyError`.

task_9.title: Support Ed25519 JWK loading and JWK algorithm inference without alg
task_9.description: The upgrade adds JWK import and export support for Ed25519 keys and allows JWK-based key loading to infer a usable default algorithm from key metadata when the JWK omits an explicit alg field. This improves EdDSA interoperability and reduces failures when consuming standard JWK documents.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Ed25519-based JWKs can be consumed through the library's JWK loading flow for EdDSA usage, and ensure that supported JWKs without an explicit algorithm can still be interpreted from their key type and curve instead of failing solely because alg is absent.

expectation.grounded: Ed25519Algorithm must support JWK conversion in both directions through to_jwk() and from_jwk(). from_jwk() must accept either a JSON string or a dictionary representing an OKP key with crv=Ed25519, return an Ed25519 public key when only x is present, and return an Ed25519 private key when d is also present. PyJWK must no longer require alg when it can infer an algorithm from JWK metadata: RSA maps to RS256, oct maps to HS256, EC maps by curve to ES256 for P-256 or absent crv, ES384 for P-384, ES512 for P-521, and ES256K for secp256k1, and OKP with crv=Ed25519 maps to EdDSA. Inputs with missing required key metadata, unsupported kty or crv values, malformed JWK JSON, missing OKP x, or invalid Ed25519 key material must be rejected with an invalid-key error.
expectation.conceptual: The library should accept standard Ed25519 JWKs for EdDSA signing and verification workflows, and it should be able to choose the correct algorithm for supported JWKs even when the JWK does not declare alg explicitly. Invalid or unsupported JWK structures should still fail clearly rather than being silently accepted.

constraints.grounded: Do not require alg when the JWK already provides enough supported metadata to infer the algorithm. Do not infer algorithms for unsupported kty or crv combinations. Do not accept non-OKP keys, non-Ed25519 OKP curves, missing OKP public material, malformed JSON input, or undecodable Ed25519 key bytes in Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk(). If a caller supplies an explicit algorithm to PyJWK, that explicit selection must continue to take precedence over inference.
constraints.conceptual: Keep backward-compatible behavior for valid existing inputs while broadening support for standards-compliant JWKs that omit alg. Reject ambiguous, malformed, or unsupported key descriptions instead of guessing.

behavior: Ed25519Algorithm exposes JWK serialization and deserialization for Ed25519 keys using OKP/Ed25519 JWK data.
Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk() accepts either string or dictionary JWK input and distinguishes public versus private Ed25519 keys by the presence of private key material.
PyJWK can construct a usable algorithm selection from JWK metadata when alg is missing, covering RSA, HMAC symmetric keys, EC keys by curve, and OKP Ed25519 keys.
OKP JWKs with crv=Ed25519 are interpreted as EdDSA by PyJWK when alg is absent.
Malformed JWK JSON, missing required JWK members, unsupported kty or crv values, wrong key family for Ed25519 parsing, and invalid Ed25519 key bytes are rejected as invalid keys.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller passes an OKP Ed25519 JWK containing x and d to Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk(), it should return a private key object that can be used for EdDSA signing.
When a caller passes an OKP Ed25519 JWK containing only x to Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk(), it should return a public key object that can be used for EdDSA verification.
When a caller serializes an Ed25519 public or private key with Ed25519Algorithm.to_jwk(), it should produce a valid OKP Ed25519 JWK representation for that key type.
When PyJWK loads a supported RSA, oct, EC, or OKP Ed25519 JWK without alg, it should choose the corresponding default algorithm from kty and crv instead of failing because alg is missing.

When PyJWK or Ed25519Algorithm.from_jwk() receives missing required metadata, unsupported key type or curve values, malformed JWK JSON, or invalid Ed25519 key material, it should reject the input with an invalid-key failure.

task_11.title: Expose PyJWK and PyJWKSet in the top-level jwt API
task_11.description: Version 2.1.0 expands the public PyJWT API by exporting the JWK model types `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` from the top-level `jwt` package. This makes those types directly importable and signals that they are part of the supported public surface for applications working with JWK data.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications upgrading to 2.1.0 can access JWK model types directly from the public `jwt` package so they can import and use `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` without relying on non-top-level module imports.

expectation.grounded: The public `jwt` package should export `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` alongside the existing top-level API. `from jwt import PyJWK, PyJWKSet` should succeed, `jwt.PyJWK` and `jwt.PyJWKSet` should be available as public attributes, and those names should be included in the package's declared public exports.
expectation.conceptual: The library should treat `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` as first-class public API types that users can import directly from `jwt`, just like other documented top-level JWT helpers and classes.

constraints.grounded: This change should add public access to `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` without removing or renaming existing top-level exports such as `PyJWT`, `PyJWS`, `PyJWKClient`, `encode`, `decode`, and related helpers. The change is limited to API exposure and should not alter the existing runtime behavior of JWT encoding, decoding, or JWK processing beyond import/accessibility.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be additive and backward-compatible: existing public imports should continue to work, while the new JWK types become directly available through the main package entry point.

behavior: The `jwt` package exposes `PyJWK` as a public top-level symbol.
The `jwt` package exposes `PyJWKSet` as a public top-level symbol.
Consumers can import `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` directly from `jwt` instead of using lower-level module paths.
The package's public export list includes `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet`, making them part of the supported top-level namespace.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer imports `PyJWK` from `jwt`, the import should succeed.
When a consumer imports `PyJWKSet` from `jwt`, the import should succeed.
When a consumer accesses `jwt.PyJWK` or `jwt.PyJWKSet`, each name should be present as a public attribute.
When a consumer relies on the package's declared public exports, `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` should be included without disrupting the availability of existing top-level API names.
